review_output: {"summary":"Not approved. This review covers the persistence foundation only, not the full WP. Several prior findings are fixed: interval receipt and session creation now use the server clock; the session row lock blocks duplicate and overlapping intervals; claim and finish lock the version before the report; and the source video is re-checked on every interval. Four MAJOR issues remain. (1) Intervals can still be deleted, which breaks the contiguity guarantee of sessions already marked complete, and the passing test suite deletes one. (2) Interval inserts read the verification, admission and live-video rows without locking them, so they race with revocation or release. Changes to those external rows also never invalidate reports. (3) Every interval updates the one version row, so ingestion serializes and every report over a version with active collection goes stale. (4) Plain UPDATEs to running/ready are still accepted and lock the report before the version, so deadlocks are still possible. There is also one MINOR gap: reports whose worker lease expires can never be reclaimed. The 56 passing tests don't cover any of these cases.","findings":[{"area":"Session completeness / evidence integrity","file":"migration: wp20_metric_interval_guard, LiveMetricInterval triggers; tests: 'deletion advances revision for cached-report invalidation'","issue":"Intervals can be updated but not deleted only in theory: UPDATE is blocked, DELETE is not. A plain DELETE on a session already marked complete leaves complete=true, finalSequence=lastSequence and a hole in the sequence. The completion check only runs when the session row is updated.","evidence":"The guard trigger only raises on TG_OP='UPDATE'. The test deletes interval-a (sequence 0) from session a after that session was closed with complete=true and finalSequence=lastSequence. It passes, and only the revision bump is checked.","confidence":0.9,"recommended_fix":"Add a BEFORE DELETE trigger on LiveMetricInterval that rejects the delete unless the parent session row is already gone (cascade from session, version, live or vendor delete). Otherwise, require a single atomic step that also sets the session back to not complete. Also block interval sequences above a non-null finalSequence, and make finalSequence immutable once set.","required_test":"After closing a session as complete, a direct DELETE of any of its intervals is rejected. Deleting the session, version, live or vendor still cascades. Inserting an interval with a sequence above finalSequence is rejected.","severity":"MAJOR","impact":"Sessions marked complete can have gaps, so reports that trust 'complete' would report watch time that the stored evidence does not contain."},{"area":"Verification/admission/video races and report invalidation","file":"migration: wp20_metric_interval_guard, wp20_metric_registration_guard","issue":"The interval guard checks FormSubmission.verificationStatus/verifiedAt, LiveViewerSession.expiresAt and Live.videoId with plain SELECTs that take no row locks. A concurrent revocation, admission release/expiry or video change can commit after the check while the interval insert still commits. Separately, none of those tables have triggers that bump sourceRevision. Revoking verification, moving a submission to another live, changing Live.formId/videoId or deleting an admission leaves ready reports and existing evidence untouched. The interval path also never re-checks Live.formId.","evidence":"The guard's JOINs on FormSubmission f, LiveViewerSession a and Live l have no FOR SHARE. Revision triggers exist only on the four LiveMetric* evidence tables. The revocation and video-change tests run one after another, not concurrently, and never check report state.","confidence":0.8,"recommended_fix":"In the guard, lock the admission, submission and live rows with FOR SHARE (or FOR KEY SHARE plus a version-side check) before validating. Add AFTER UPDATE/DELETE triggers on FormSubmission (verification fields, liveId), Live (videoId, formId) and LiveViewerSession that lock the affected versions in the same order as ingestion (session then version) and bump their sourceRevision. Alternatively, make revocation record a tombstone that reports exclude.","required_test":"Two-connection tests. (a) Transaction A revokes verification and holds the transaction open; transaction B inserts an interval; after A commits, B fails (or the interval is rejected). (b) The same for an admission DELETE and a Live.videoId change. (c) A ready report becomes stale after verification is revoked or the live's video changes.","severity":"MAJOR","impact":"Viewers whose verification was revoked or whose admission was released can still add evidence, and cached reports keep counting them."},{"area":"Throughput / report liveness","file":"migration: wp20_metric_evidence_changed, wp20_metric_report_invalidate, wp20_metric_report_claim/finish","issue":"Every interval insert (one per viewer every ≤5 s) updates the single LiveMetricVersion row and holds that row lock until commit. It also runs a scan that marks reports stale. As a result, all ingestion for a live serializes on one row and produces heavy dead-row churn. Every report for that version is invalidated by every new interval, even one outside the report's time window. Claim and finish take FOR UPDATE on the same row. So while collection is active, a report can rarely reach ready and workers will keep requeueing it.","evidence":"In the concurrency test, all 12 sessions bump the revision by 12, and the parallel report always ends up 'stale'. The test asserts that stale outcome as expected behavior.","confidence":0.85,"recommended_fix":"Track revisions per time bucket (e.g. a per-window revision row, or invalidation keyed by the overlap of wallEndAt with the report window). Alternatively, build reports from an immutable snapshot of closed windows and invalidate only on deletions or revocations. Move the per-interval revision bump off the shared version row, for example with sharded counters or an append-only change log.","required_test":"A load test with ≥500 concurrent sessions sending intervals for 60 s, run against a disposable DB. Measure p95 interval insert latency and lock waits on LiveMetricVersion. Show that a report over a window that has already closed reaches ready while ingestion continues.","severity":"MAJOR","impact":"Ingestion slows as audiences grow, and report generation stalls during the very events it is meant to measure."},{"area":"Lock ordering enforcement","file":"migration: wp20_metric_report_guard; tests: 'source changes invalidate report and its lease'","issue":"The required order (version, then report) is only a convention. The database still accepts a plain UPDATE of a report to running/ready. That UPDATE locks the report row first and then takes FOR SHARE on the version, the reverse of ingestion (version FOR UPDATE, then a report UPDATE inside the invalidation trigger). The result can be a deadlock that aborts interval ingestion. The test suite itself uses a plain UPDATE to set running.","evidence":"The guard has no check that the change came through claim/finish. The test sets status='running' with $executeRawUnsafe. Taking FOR SHARE inside one transaction and FOR UPDATE later in the same transaction can also deadlock against a concurrent upgrader.","confidence":0.7,"recommended_fix":"Have claim/finish set a transaction-local flag (set_config('wp20.report_writer','on',true)). In the guard, reject transitions to running/ready unless the flag is set. Alternatively, make claim/finish SECURITY DEFINER under a dedicated owner and revoke UPDATE on the report table from the application role. Also add a create-report function that takes FOR UPDATE on the version instead of FOR SHARE.","required_test":"A plain UPDATE setting a report to running or ready is rejected. Run a concurrent plain report UPDATE against interval inserts, and run concurrent create-then-claim transactions; show no deadlock (40P01) occurs.","severity":"MAJOR","impact":"A later API that uses the ORM directly would bring back the deadlocks fixed in the prior round, aborting ingestion. Nothing in the schema stops it."},{"area":"Report lease recovery","file":"migration: wp20_metric_report_claim","issue":"Claim only accepts status='queued'. A report left 'running' after its worker crashes and the lease expires can never be reclaimed, and attempts has no upper bound. The claim index on leaseExpiresAt suggests reclaiming was intended but never implemented.","evidence":"The claim UPDATE filters only on status='queued' and has no path for running reports with leaseExpiresAt <= clock_timestamp(). There is no transition to 'failed'.","confidence":0.75,"recommended_fix":"Allow claiming when status='running' and leaseExpiresAt <= clock_timestamp(), still locking the version first and re-checking that inputRevision is current. Mark the report failed after N attempts.","required_test":"A report whose lease has expired can be claimed by a different worker. Finish from the original worker then returns 0. The report becomes failed after the maximum number of attempts.","severity":"MINOR","impact":"If a worker crashes, its reports stay stuck in 'running' until someone fixes them by hand."}]}
